subject: Business and Entrepreneurship
text: Read the case and answer the following questions. In 2022, two teachers launched an ed-tech platform with the vision of making skill-based learning more accessible to college students and young professionals. Their mission was to bridge the gap between traditional education and industry needs by offering short practical courses in areas like digital marketing, coding, and financial literacy. The platform started with a few online modules but soon expanded to include live workshops, mentorship programs, and certification tie-ups with universities. Their business plan highlighted student-focused research, user-friendly technology, and clear revenue forecasts. To raise funds for platform development and marketing, the founders turned to crowdfunding, where they gained both financial support and a community of learners eager to join their initiative. Questions (4 Marks Each) How successful do you think expanding from online modules to live workshops and certifications will be? Provide reasoning. Explain how crowdfunding contributed to both financing and learner community building for the ed-tech platform. Analyze the existing components of the business plan and suggest additional elements that could further strengthen the startup’s strategy and execution.

subject: Business and Entrepreneurship
text: Read the case and answer the following questions. Radhika, a young entrepreneur, launched Herbal Bloom, a startup producing eco-friendly herbal skincare products with the aim of offering chemical-free, affordable skincare while creating employment opportunities for rural women. Initially self-financed, she later attracted an angel investor after preparing a comprehensive business plan. Her venture was supported by a committed team, high-quality raw materials, and a skilled women workforce. Favorable government policies for small businesses, growing consumer interest in organic products, and the effective use of social media marketing and e-commerce platforms helped the brand gain traction, especially among the youth who were increasingly aware of environmentally friendly products. Within three years, Herbal Bloom expanded into metro cities and formed partnerships with online marketplaces. However, as the business grew, it began to encounter strong competition from established cosmetic brands, leading Radhika to explore strategic partnerships with larger companies to fuel further expansion. Questions (4 Marks Each) Conduct a SWOT analysis of Herbal Bloom based on the case. Discuss how Radhika’s entrepreneurial traits and funding decisions contributed to the firm’s growth. Suggest whether entering into a strategic alliance is a suitable corporate strategy for Herbal Bloom’s future growth.
